name: Audio-rate AM for wave-shaping and FM/ring-like texture
goal: Create complex cinematic textures with audio-rate amplitude modulation: feed a soft waveform (sine/triangle/saw) into a VCA and modulate that VCA at audio rate from another waveform of the same oscillator (self AM / new wave shapes) or a second oscillator (complex sidebands); put the AM depth under an envelope or LFO VCA so dynamics evolve—often reducing the need for a filter.

source.title: Don’t forget about this old trick – Audio rate amplitude modulation (AM)

prerequisites: Synth/modular with at least one osc (preferably dual waveforms), VCA(s), envelope/LFO; optional second oscillator

outputs.name: am_texture_voice
outputs.description: Audio-rate AM voice with dynamic depth control

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Delta vs fm-carrier-modulator-ratio-basics and keysol-venus-noise-audiorate-filter-texture: this is AM into a VCA (wave-shaping/sidebands), not FM ratios or noise→filter.

steps.action: Recall ordinary AM: envelopes/LFOs into a VCA control volume or mod depth. Audio-rate AM instead uses an audio-frequency signal as the VCA CV so amplitude changes happen inside each cycle → new wave shapes / sidebands.

Self-AM wave-shaping: send a soft shape (sine/triangle) into VCA1 audio input; modulate VCA1 with an alternate waveform of the same oscillator (e.g. square). Use a separate final VCA for note volume so VCA1 is only the shaper.
steps.expect: Carrier morphs into a new harmonic shape

steps.action: Dynamic depth: route the modulator through another VCA controlled by the same envelope (or an LFO) that also opens the amp VCA—so AM depth blooms with the note instead of staying static.
steps.expect: Timbre opens with dynamics; filter optional

steps.action: Two-oscillator AM: modulate VCA1 with a second oscillator at a different frequency for more complex signals (often both pitches audible). Experiment with VCA bias/response for softer vs harder AM.

Expand: mix multiple alternate waves through VCAs before they modulate the carrier; replace envelope with LFO for continuous wave-shape motion. Keep levels modest for pads; follow with gentle filter/space FX if needed.
steps.expect: Evolving AM texture suitable for cinematic beds

verification: Disabling audio-rate mod returns plain carrier wave
Envelope on mod-depth VCA changes brightness/complexity over the note
Second-osc AM produces more complex sidebands than self-AM
